overview: Rapid review reported with PRISMA 2020 and SWiM, updating the 2023 systematic review from January 2022 and synthesising strategies that increase uptake of bereavement follow-up offered by palliative care services, with every shortcut declared.
population: Bereaved relatives or close friends offered bereavement follow-up by inpatient hospice, community or hospital palliative care services; studies in any country published in English from 2012 to October 2026.
exposure: Strategies intended to increase uptake: proactive personal contact, timing of the first offer, mode of the offer (telephone, text message, letter, in person), risk-based targeting, and outreach adapted for men, interpreter needs, distance or cultural groups.
procedures: The librarian searches three bibliographic databases and two grey-literature sources from January 2022 to October 2026 and checks the references of the 2023 review. One reviewer screens titles and abstracts; the social worker independently screens a random 20 percent, and disagreements are discussed. One reviewer screens full texts and a second checks every exclusion. One reviewer extracts design, setting, strategy, comparator, both uptake definitions and results by sex, language and distance; the second checks every uptake figure. Risk of bias uses a short checklist matched to design, and certainty is rated per strategy with GRADE.

outcomes.name: Uptake of bereavement support
outcomes.measure: Proportion of relatives offered follow-up who accepted support, and proportion who attended at least one session, extracted separately
outcomes.timing: As reported, up to 13 months after the death
outcomes.why: The service outcome the board must decide on, and the outcome the current programme fails.

outcomes.name: Grief and wellbeing of bereaved relatives
outcomes.measure: Any validated grief or wellbeing scale reported by included studies, summarised without pooling
outcomes.timing: 6 to 13 months after the death, as reported
outcomes.why: Uptake matters only if support helps; the review records whether any study measured it.

outcomes.name: Reach of the first contact
outcomes.measure: Proportion of eligible relatives reached by the first offer
outcomes.why: Separates a strategy that reaches more families from one that persuades more of those reached.

outcomes.name: Distress or complaints about unsolicited contact
outcomes.measure: Reported complaints, requests to stop contact or distress linked to proactive or text contact
outcomes.why: Proactive contact can intrude on grief; the board needs to know whether this was measured.

feasibility: Week 1 protocol and search, weeks 2 to 4 screening, weeks 5 and 6 extraction and appraisal, week 7 synthesis, week 8 board report; two librarian days and about 20 percent of screening by the social worker, as approved.
biasMitigation: Strategy groups and both uptake definitions fixed in the protocol before screening
Random 20 percent of title and abstract decisions screened independently by a second reviewer
Every uptake figure checked by a second reviewer
Shortcuts reported with their likely effect on the findings

biasFlags.label: Single-reviewer screening
biasFlags.note: Partly checked by the 20 percent sample; reported as a limitation.

biasFlags.label: English-language limit
biasFlags.note: May miss service evaluations in other languages.

biasFlags.label: Publication bias toward positive service evaluations
biasFlags.note: Grey literature search and a statement of the direction this bias would push.

flags: One primary outcome with two pre-specified definitions; one process and one balancing measure
parsimony.simplestPath: Update one existing synthesis, extract one outcome in two definitions, and group studies by five strategies.

theoreticalFramework: None beyond PRISMA 2020 and SWiM; a behavioural framework would not change what is extracted in eight weeks.
summary: Eight-week rapid review updating the 2023 synthesis; one primary outcome in two definitions, one secondary, one process and one balancing measure.
